name: Equestrian Committee Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  JANUARY 22, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City
Hall.

2.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Ciarolla, Griggs, Harik, Martin, Nilsen,
  Shinn, Silvano, and Schachter
  Committee Members Absent:  Medawar
  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 28, 2023
  MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER HARIK to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF AUGUST 28, 2023, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  NONE.

5.  BUSINESS ITEMS
A.  EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that staff was looking to resume the Equine
  Emergency Preparedness Subcommittee meetings and wanted to confirm the
  current members of the subcommittee. Committee Members Shinn, Nilsen, Griggs,
  and Silvano confirmed their participation.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 22, 2024
   Supervisor Pinuelas asked if there was any interest in the vacant subcommittee
  position created by Committee Member Robinson’s departure. Supervisor
  Pinuelas confirmed that four members are sufficient for the subcommittee in
  response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an overview of equine emergency preparedness
  accomplishments to date and shared that the City website incorporates equine
  emergency preparedness information such as the listing of local veterinarians,
  horse haulers, and medical supply recommendations.

  MEMBER SHINN requested that another training be held for sheriff deputies to
  familiarize them with the trail areas where issues can occur and stated that they
  need to have both small and big halters in their vehicles. MEMBER SHINN
  responded that it had been a while since the last training was held, in response to
  CHAIR SCHACHTER. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the subcommittee could
  discuss this further, and that staff would also work to get this item started, in
  response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  The Committee agreed that Members Shinn, Nilsen, Griggs, and Silvano would
  continue on the subcommittee.

B.  EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired about a previous half-day fee for clinics. Supervisor
  Pinuelas responded that the half-day fee had been eliminated in 2022, upon
  recommendation of the Equestrian Committee.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER expressed concern that trainers were not reserving the
  arena for half-day clinics and that she considered the $212 full-day arena rental
  cost to be high. She also expressed concern that because of not reserving the
  arenas, the City was not being compensated for these clinics, which are not put on
  the City calendar to inform the public about use, and the arenas are not prepared
  for the clinics.

  MEMBER SILVANO stated that she would be opposed to a half-day rental rate as
  they require the same arena preparation time as a full day rental and because the
  arena needs to be closed right after preparation until the day and time of the clinic
  resulting in a full day closure.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 22, 2024
   Discussion ensued regarding clinics being held without reservations, clinicians not
  allowing the public to use the arenas during said clinics, and the difficulty of
  enforcement.
  MEMBER GRIGGS suggested allowing reservation of a ring without preparation
  for no fee.
  MEMBER SHINN stated that she believed the fees are low. MEMBER MARTIN
  concurred.
  MEMBER HARIK stated that she felt the bigger concern is people not paying and
  using the arena for the entire day without allowing public access.
  MEMBER NILSEN stated that it sounded like an enforcement issue and feels the
  current rate is reasonable.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER affirmed that there would be no change and stated that
  trainers would be encouraged to pay full price for the rentals.

6.  STAFF ITEMS

A.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM PROJECT UPDATE
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that City staff have the portable restroom building
  ready for installation but was informed of a new Los Angeles County Public Health
  requirement that needs to be resolved before installation causing a project delay.
  She reported that staff has been working with the Los Angeles County Public
  Health Department to provide the necessary documentation. She stated that staff
  received some of the revised submittal information needed the previous Friday
  from the Los Angeles County Sanitation District, who owns the site, and that staff
  would be resubmitting what is needed with hopes to install the restroom the
  following month.

B.  DISCUSSION OF LANDFILL TRAIL ACCESS (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR SCHACHTER introduced the item explaining that she had received
  concerns regarding interactions between a Los Angeles County Sanitation District
  landfill employee and unleashed dog owners and equestrians using trails in the
  middle of the landfill. She explained that this agenda item was intended to raise
  consciousness and provide an opportunity to remind riders and dog walkers about
  the landfill rules that require the public to use the perimeter route of the landfill and
  to keep dogs on leash. CHAIR SCHACHTER clarified that privileges are not being
  revoked by the District, but that everyone should follow the rules to prevent that
  from happening.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 22, 2024
   Superintendent Goldsmith reported that he also spoke with District employees at
  the landfill and reiterated that this item is not about closing of the landfill trails. He
  noted that when the Cal Water project was taking place, the County temporarily
  changed where riding was permitted. He explained the landfill is not City property
  and that riding is only allowed on the landfill’s upper deck and outer perimeter.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the interior surface maintenance roads are
  off limits to the public, dogs, and horses. He shared an image of County installed
  signage and expressed the need to stay on the upper deck of the outer perimeter
  and not to go through the middle of the landfill. Superintendent Goldsmith also
  shared a map of the landfill which indicated the outer perimeter and reiterated that
  there was no discussion of the closure of any trails.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that County staff and contractors often work on
  weekends, in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he would work with County staff to see about
  creating banners to educate the public regarding where access is allowed and not
  allowed.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER explained that people got used to being able to go through
  the middle of the landfill during the Cal Water project but reiterated the need to go
  back to only using the outer perimeter. She also shared that the County approved
  use of the outer perimeter for recreational use.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the County just wants to ensure no one is
  on the roads in the middle of the landfill, in response to Audience Member Sharon
  Yarber regarding the asphalt road on the upper deck.

  Peter Weber Equestrian Center Concessionaire Gil Houle commented on
  interactions between members of the public and County staff.

  Audience Member Nancy Michalski commented about unleashed dogs and
  enforcement.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER explained that the City can educate via social media and
  community newsletter and invited the public to submit other ideas to her or
  Supervisor Pinuelas. Discussion ensued regarding unleashed dogs and difficulties
  of enforcement.

  Audience Member Kelly Yates thanked the Committee and Superintendent
  Goldsmith for their work and commented on the importance of communication.

  Audience Member Candy Young suggested the Peter Weber Equestrian Center
  concessionaires put out messaging to their participants regarding the landfill

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 22, 2024
   access. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that he had spoken to them and they
  will be sending information out via email and he would send out a Nixle message
  in addition to creating an informational flyer.

  Audience Member Anna Chu inquired about the status of a designated task force
  created in 2004 with the LA County Sanitation District and the Sierra Project for
  the purpose of permanently restoring the landfill to recreation use. CHAIR
  SCHACHTER responded that no items regarding that task force had come before
  the Park and Activities Commission or the Equestrian Committee.

C.  E-BIKES ON BRIDLE TRAILS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that A-frame signage has been placed at key points
  on the trail to educate those using trails as to the restriction of e-bikes, bikes, and
  wheeled vehicles on the trails. She noted that they were designed to be portable
  allowing staff to move them to different locations to help draw attention to them.
  She added that staff was working with the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School
  District and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department-Lomita Station to
  understand how the Sheriff’s Department can partner with the schools to educate
  the students and families. Supervisor Pinuelas also shared that the Sheriff's
  Department would be patrolling the trails with a Polaris once their training
  concluded. She added that staff would continue to explore other options for
  education and keep the Committee updated.

  MEMBER GRIGGS expressed concern regarding Polaris vehicles being on the
  trails. CHAIR SCHACHTER shared they are used in Palos Verdes Estates and
  MEMBER CIAROLLA stated they have been used on the Chandler Preserve.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that City vehicles are on the trails when needed
  and that the Polaris would be used to access trails by public safety and would not
  be a daily occurrence nor at high speeds.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that the deputies could be educated regarding horses
  and concerns about safety.

  Discussion ensued regarding bike lanes and issues with e-bike users and
  mountain bikers.

  Audience Member Julie Ramstead commented on e-bike users at Ernie Howlett
  Park.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER recommended the public visit the City website to sign up for
  the City newsletter, announcements and Nixle alerts.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 22, 2024
   Audience Member Susan Fairchild commented on e-bike issues and the need for
  the issue to be resolved at the state level.

D.  SHARING THE TRAILS SAFETY OUTREACH VIDEO SERIES

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that staff was working to get videos filmed on
  February 5, and would be working with some of the Equestrian Committee
  members to assist. She reported that once filmed and edited, staff would post the
  videos on social media and the City website.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that video topics included reminders that wheeled
  vehicles such as bikes are not allowed on the trails and that dogs must be leashed
  as well as what to do when joggers or walkers encounter a horse on the trail, in
  response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

E.  2023 CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEF

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.

  MEMBER MARTIN requested the event not be scheduled on the same date as the
  Ranch Life event.

  MEMBER MARTIN stated that the Raffle Ride started at 8:00 am and the
  gymkhana events at 10:00 am, in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  MEMBER SHINN stated that the equestrian events did not have any Raffle Ride
  participants this year and only had drill team participants, so the gymkhana events
  went quickly, in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  MEMBER SHINN stated that the event went well and that the Stick Horse Races
  continue to be a hit. MEMBER SHINN requested a list of past sponsors 2-3 months
  prior to the event to solicit more sponsorships this year.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER noted the event budget was higher this year and that there
  were just as many in attendance and that the event seemed very popular.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that guided horse rides and axe throwing were new this
  year, with the guided horse rides being very popular but alternatives to axe
  throwing are being considered as that activity was not very popular.

F.  2024 MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 22, 2024
   Supervisor Pinuelas reported that this year’s event is scheduled for Saturday, May
  11, and that the Scouts would be returning to host their traditional pancake
  breakfast.

G.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that staff was working to schedule the Carol Dean
  Porter and the Jan Ball dedication ceremonies in February. She stated that staff
  was coordinating with the Peter Weber Equestrian Center to determine the location
  for the Jan Ball bench as well as potential dates for a dedication ceremony.
  Supervisor Pinuelas said she would inform the Committee once the dates for each
  dedication ceremony had been set.

H.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  CHAIR SCHACHTER thanked Superintendent Goldsmith and his staff for their
  work and noted that the issues are not only equestrian related but include issues
  regarding trails, trees and more.

  MEMBER GRIGGS inquired about the status of the Dapplegray round pen.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that sand had been delivered and it was
  planned to be addressed the following week.

I.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

7.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHACHTER ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:07 pm.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,
